target.title: [codex] fix gateway restart-required reload drift
target.body:
## Summary

Read-only runtime-config drift diagnostics for gateway health. `openclaw health` (JSON and text) now reports when the running gateway's live config has drifted from the disk file on restart-required paths (model/provider/auth), so an operator can see that a disk-side repair or rotation is waiting on a restart instead of trusting a green health snapshot.

- Adds a `runtimeConfig` block to the health summary: `state: "ok" | "drift" | "unknown"`, live/disk `agents.defaults.model` labels, and the list of drifted paths (tracked: `agents.defaults.model`, `agents.defaults.models`, `agents.list`, `models`, `gateway.auth`, `auth.profiles`, `auth.order`, `secrets.providers`).
- Distinguishes unreadable/missing/invalid disk config (`state: "unknown"` with a generic message for non-admin callers) from real drift, and renders both drift and unknown states in text output.
- Gates config fingerprints (`liveSourceFingerprint`, `diskSourceFingerprint`) and the detailed disk-read error (which can contain the local config path or a parse-error excerpt) to admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) callers.
- Recomputes the drift summary on gateway health cache hits inside `mergeCachedHealthRuntimeState`, mirroring the existing delivery-queue / hot-reload-status recompute pattern, so read-scoped callers always see fresh drift state.

This PR is observability only. The hot-mode restart-required reload behavior change (honoring the restart plan instead of warn-and-keep) is intentionally NOT in this diff; it lives in the companion PR #89517 so behavior and diagnostics can be reviewed and landed independently. An earlier revision of this PR carried both concerns; they were split on 2026-06-08.

## What Problem This Solves

When `gateway.reload.mode` is `hot`, restart-required config changes (model/provider/auth) are warn-and-keep: the gateway logs `config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (...)` and keeps running on the old pinned runtime config. Nothing user-visible reported that state afterwards: `openclaw health` said everything was ok while the gateway served stale model routing or an old `gateway.auth` token that no longer matched disk. Operators debugging "my config change did nothing" had only a single gateway log line to find.

This revision also resolves the outstanding ClawSweeper P1 on this PR: `openclaw health` connects least-privilege at `operator.read` and is served from the non-sensitive 60s health cache, so a cached "ok" could mask drift that appeared right after the cache was filled. The previous head gated a cache bypass on `operator.admin`, which never fired for the read-scoped CLI. Instead of extending the bypass, the drift summary is now recomputed on every cache hit (scope-aware; fingerprints stay admin-only) and the admin bypass was deleted -- no cache bypass remains.

## Evidence

All commands below were run at head `4229b9999d` (this branch rebased onto `upstream/main` at `22376d80e1`) in a worktree on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Node 24.

Unit/regression tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/health.snapshot.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts
  -> Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 49 passed (49)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
  -> Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 525 passed (525)
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                      -> clean
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json   -> clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <7 changed files>                        -> clean
oxfmt --check <7 changed files>                                      -> clean
```

New tests in this revision (`src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts`):

- `recomputes runtime-config drift on cache hits so read-scoped callers see fresh drift` -- cached "ok" + drift recompute -> `operator.read` cache hit (`{ cached: true }` respond flag asserted) returns `state: "drift"` with no fingerprints.
- `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute so fingerprints stay admin-only` -- same cache-hit path with `operator.admin` receives fingerprints; background refresh still runs.
- `drops a stale cached runtime-config summary when the recompute returns none`.

Live behavior proof (redacted, exact head): see the `Real behavior proof` section below -- a sandbox gateway built from this head shows the ok -> drift transition on the plain, non-verbose, read-scoped `openclaw health` path after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `mode: "hot"`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: plain `openclaw health` (least-privilege `operator.read`, both JSON and text) reports `runtimeConfig.state: "drift"` with `driftPaths: ["gateway.auth"]` after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"`, including when the response is served from the 60s health cache; fingerprints are omitted for read-scoped callers.

Real environment tested: sandbox gateway on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), dist built from this branch at head `4229b9999d` content, launched with `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 28934`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config: `gateway.mode: "local"`, `gateway.auth: { mode: "token", token: "sandbox-token-OLD" }`, `gateway.reload: { mode: "hot", debounceMs: 100 }`, `agents.defaults.model: "openai/gpt-5.5"`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node dist/index.js health --json                 # call 1, fills the health cache
sed -i.bak 's/sandbox-token-OLD/sandbox-token-NEW/' $SANDBOX/openclaw.json
sleep 4
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health --json   # call 2, ~40s after call 1
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health          # text mode
```

Evidence after fix:

- Call 1 (before rotation): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "ok", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5"}` -- no fingerprint fields on the read-scoped path.
- Gateway reload log after `sed`:
  ```
  [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.auth.token)
  [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.auth.token)
  ```
- Call 2 (after rotation, inside the 60s `HEALTH_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` window of call 1, i.e. the cache-hit merge path): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "drift", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "driftPaths": ["gateway.auth"], "message": "Live gateway runtime config differs from disk for model/provider/auth paths; restart is required or pending."}` -- no fingerprint fields.
- Text mode: `Runtime config: warning (live gateway differs from disk for gateway.auth; restart required or pending; live=openai/gpt-5.5 disk=openai/gpt-5.5)`.

Observed result after fix: the ok -> drift transition is visible on the normal read-scoped `openclaw health` path immediately after the disk change, with hot mode still warn-and-keep (live gateway kept accepting `sandbox-token-OLD`); the earlier caveat about the in-process snapshot-refresh handler masking external edits no longer reproduces on current main.

What was not tested: admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) live output with fingerprints (covered by unit tests `surfaces model/provider runtime config drift ... in sensitive snapshots` and `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute`); live drift on the non-auth tracked paths such as `agents.defaults.model` or `auth.profiles` (covered by unit tests); the `{ cached: true }` respond flag is not printed by the CLI, so cache-hit routing of call 2 is established by the 60s window timing plus the deterministic handler tests.
